tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

The call ends your run, so do everything else first and put everything your caller needs in that one report. It is not a messaging channel: do not use it for progress updates or questions.

Only a report delivered through SubagentHandback reaches your caller; plain text you write at the end of your run is NOT delivered. There is no recipient parameter: the report can only go to your caller.

# Estimating the gold grader's error with a second grader

Draft 0.2 — 2026-10-13. Closes the boundary of [judge_shared_error_measurement.md](judge_shared_error_measurement.md) §5: Proposition 2 inverts
gold noise at a *known* flip rate \(\eta\); here \(\eta\) is estimated from a second independent grader, exactly. 0.2 adds the exact sampling law of
\(\hat\eta_1\) (§6) and the asymmetric Dawid–Skene model with its inversion (§7). Files: `src/spiral_ln/evaluation_gold_calibration.py`,
`tests/test_evaluation_gold_calibration.py` (84 tests), `output/evaluation_gold_calibration/gold_v0_2.json` (40 checks, source hashes, exact
fractions, floats under `headline`). No model, judge or grader was called; every number is a `Fraction`; the judge module's tails and maps are reused.

```powershell
$env:PYTHONPATH = "src"; python scripts/verify_evaluation_gold_calibration.py --sampling-size 400 --sampling-size 742 --output output/evaluation_gold_calibration/gold_v0_2.json
python -m pytest tests/test_evaluation_gold_calibration.py -q
```

## 1. Model

True label \(Y\in\{0,1\}\), \(\pi=\Pr[Y=1]\). Three raters report \(Y\) flipped independently given \(Y\), each with one symmetric error rate: the gold
grader \(G_1\) (\(\eta_1\)), a second grader \(G_2\) (\(\eta_2\)) and the controller's own answer \(X_C\) (error \(1-a\)). The judge is excluded: its verdict
implies a label that equals \(Y\) iff \(J=1\), and that label is conditionally independent of \(X_C\) given \(Y\) iff \(\varepsilon_0=\varepsilon\), i.e. iff
\(\varepsilon_1=\varepsilon\) — axiom A2, the hypothesis under test. Write \(\tau=1-2\pi\), \(d_i=1-2e_i\), and for \(S\subseteq\{1,2,3\}\) the Walsh
coefficient \(\hat p_S=E\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{X_i}\).

**Proposition 1.** \(\hat p_S=\tau^{[|S|\text{ odd}]}\prod_{i\in S}d_i\). *Proof.* \(E[(-1)^{X_i}\mid Y]=(-1)^Y d_i\); conditional independence multiplies;
\(E[(-1)^{kY}]\) is \(\tau\) for odd \(k\) and \(1\) for even. \(\square\) So the marginal bias \(M_i=\Pr[X_i=0]-\Pr[X_i=1]=\tau d_i\), the pair polarity
\(\kappa_{ij}=2A_{ij}-1=d_id_j\) with \(A_{ij}=\Pr[X_i=X_j]=1-e_i-e_j+2e_ie_j\), and the parity bias \(P=\hat p_{123}=\tau d_1d_2d_3\). (`walsh_coefficients`,
`three_rater_model`; checked against enumeration of the \(2^4\) latent cells \((Y,X_1,X_2,X_3)\) on a grid of 750 rational parameter points.)

## 2. Identities and identifiability

**Proposition 2.** If \(\kappa_{jk}\ne0\) then \((1-2e_i)^2=\kappa_{ij}\kappa_{ik}/\kappa_{jk}\). *Proof.* \(d_id_j\,d_id_k/(d_jd_k)=d_i^2\). \(\square\) (`polarity_squares`.)
From the agreement rates alone the three \(\kappa\)'s determine the three squares and nothing more; the root's sign is fixed by the convention
\(e_i<\tfrac12\), which needs every \(\kappa>0\). That convention is a modelling assumption, not a finding: \((\tau,d)\mapsto(-\tau,-d)\) — every rater worse
than chance and the prior swapped — leaves every \(\hat p_S\) unchanged (`three_rater_model(1-π, 1-e)` equals `three_rater_model(π, e)` on the whole
grid). A rater at chance (\(d_i=0\)) zeroes both of its polarities and leaves the other two with one equation for two unknowns (`polarity_squares`
raises). Exactly one or three negative \(\kappa\)'s fit no symmetric model of any sign.

The root is irrational in general, so three exact operations replace it (`error_rate_from_square`, `error_rate_at_most`, `error_rate_bracket`):
(a) exact recovery when the square is a perfect square, which at expected counts with rational rates it always is — the fixture's
\(\kappa=(\tfrac{12}{25},\tfrac{12}{25},\tfrac9{25})\) give squares \(\tfrac{16}{25},\tfrac9{25},\tfrac9{25}\), hence \(\eta_1=\tfrac1{10}\), \(\eta_2=\tfrac15\), \(a=\tfrac45\); (b) membership:
\(\eta_1\le\eta_0\) iff \(d_1\ge1-2\eta_0\) iff (for \(\eta_0<\tfrac12\)) \(\kappa_{12}\kappa_{13}/\kappa_{23}\ge(1-2\eta_0)^2\), a rational comparison; (c) a bracket of width
\(2^{-16}\) by bisection on (b), or from \(r=\lfloor2^{16}\sqrt S\rfloor=\mathrm{isqrt}\lfloor4^{16}S\rfloor\) (`root_bracket`, exact integer arithmetic). Gradient of
the estimate (`eta_gradient`): \(\partial\eta_1/\partial\kappa=(-d_1/4\kappa_{12},\,-d_1/4\kappa_{13},\,+d_1/4\kappa_{23})\), at the fixture \((-\tfrac5{12},-\tfrac5{12},\tfrac59)\);
per agreement rate twice that.

## 3. Testable constraints and falsifiers

The \(2^3\) cells have 7 degrees of freedom; the model has 4 parameters \((\tau,d_1,d_2,d_3)\), and its exact Jacobian has rank 4 wherever every
\(d_i\ne0\) (the three pair rows have determinant \(-2d_1d_2d_3\) on the \(d\) columns; `model_jacobian_rank`). So there are exactly three constraints:

**Proposition 3.** \(M_1\kappa_{23}=M_2\kappa_{13}=M_3\kappa_{12}=P\). *Proof.* Each side is \(\tau d_1d_2d_3\). \(\square\) Conversely, a table with all \(\kappa>0\),
squares in \([0,1]\), \(M_i^2\le d_i^2\) and these three equalities is the image of exactly one parameter point with every \(e_i<\tfrac12\) (set \(d_i\) from
Proposition 2, \(\tau=M_1/d_1\); the equalities make \(M_i/d_i\) agree; argued here, not separately checked in code). In cell terms: for every \(x\),
\(p(x)+p(\bar x)=\tfrac14\big(1+\sum_{i<j}\kappa_{ij}\chi_{ij}(x)\big)\) holds for *any* distribution, so the complementary-pair sums carry no constraint; the
content sits in the imbalances \(p(x)-p(\bar x)=\tfrac14\big(\sum_iM_i\chi_i(x)+P\chi_{123}(x)\big)\), whose parity term must equal each \(M_i\kappa_{jk}\). **At a
balanced prior every odd coefficient vanishes and the equalities read \(0=0\):** the check has no power against grader dependence when
\(\pi=\tfrac12\) (`vacuous_at_balanced_prior`).

Falsifiers (`model_constraints`), all exact: a table with \(\kappa=(-\tfrac15,\tfrac15,\tfrac15)\) (one negative: no sign assignment); a table with
\(\kappa=(\tfrac{12}{25},\tfrac{12}{25},\tfrac1{25})\), whose implied \((1-2\eta_1)^2=\tfrac{144}{25}>1\); and a dependent grader. If \(G_2\) copies \(G_1\) with probability
\(\rho\) and grades independently otherwise, then \(r_1=r_2=-\tau d_C\,\rho\,4\eta_1(1-\eta_1)\) and \(r_3=0\), where \(r_i=M_i\kappa_{jk}-P\) (`copy_grader_residual`;
checked for \(\rho\in\{0,\tfrac14,\tfrac12,\tfrac34,1\}\) at the fixture prior and for four \(\rho\) at each of five priors): the failing constraints name the
dependent pair, and any \(\rho>0\) is detected whenever \(\tau\ne0\), \(a\ne\tfrac12\) and \(0<\eta_1<1\). With asymmetric errors the model has 7 parameters,
the just-identified Dawid–Skene case of §7, which has no such constraint.

## 4. Pipeline (`calibrate`)

Input: the \(2^4\) record of \((x_C,v_J,g_1,g_2)\) on \(m\) sealed items. (1) Marginalise over the judge to the label table \((g_1,g_2,x_C)\); run the
constraint check. (2) \(\kappa\)'s, squares, \(\hat\eta_1,\hat\eta_2,\hat a\) by Proposition 2, exact or bracketed. (3) Tabulate the judge note's \(2\times2\)
against \(G_1\): \(a',\varepsilon',w=W_1'/m\). (4) Invert Proposition 2 of the judge note at \(\eta=\hat\eta_1\) (`gold_noise_inverse`, reused) to
\((\hat a,\hat\varepsilon,\hat\varepsilon_1)\); the inverted \(\hat a\) equals the identity's \(\hat a\) on every table with all \(\kappa>0\), since \(\hat d_1\hat d_C=\kappa_{1C}\) exactly.
(5) `expected_table` at the recovered rates, rounded half-up (`rounded_table`), then `independence_p_value` (declared \(\varepsilon\), or the plug-in
flagged), `fisher_p_value`, `ceiling_p_value`, `clopper_pearson_contains`. When \(\hat\eta_1\) is a bracket, every inverted rate is monotone in \(\eta\)
(\(da/d\eta=(2a'-1)/(1-2\eta)^2\), \(d\varepsilon/d\eta=(2\varepsilon'-1)/(1-2\eta)^2\), and the next line), so the bracket ends map to ends and (4)–(5) run at both.

**Sensitivity.** Substituting \(a-\varepsilon=(a'-\varepsilon')/(1-2\eta)\) and \(1-a=(1-a'-\eta)/(1-2\eta)\) into the note's inversion gives one rational function
\(\varepsilon_1(\eta)=\dfrac{w(1-2\eta)-\eta(a'-\varepsilon')}{1-a'-\eta}\) (`inverted_eps1`, equal to the judge module's value on the grid). Numerator and denominator
are affine, so with \(K=w(2a'-1)-(a'-\varepsilon')(1-a')\), free of \(\eta\): \(\dfrac{d\varepsilon_1}{d\eta}=\dfrac{K}{(1-a'-\eta)^2}\) and exactly
\(\varepsilon_1(\eta+\Delta)-\varepsilon_1(\eta)=\dfrac{\Delta K}{(1-a'-\eta)(1-a'-\eta-\Delta)}\) (`eps1_sensitivity`, `eps1_displacement`; checked against direct re-inversion).
At the fixture \(K=-\tfrac{64}{625}\), \(1-a'-\eta=\tfrac4{25}\): **\(d\varepsilon_1/d\eta=-4\)** for the independent judge and \(-\tfrac52\) for the shared one. Overestimating
\(\eta\) by \(\Delta\) lowers \(\hat\varepsilon_1\) by about \(4\Delta\) (more of the wrong-wrong cell is attributed to flips); \(\Delta=\tfrac1{100}\) moves it by exactly
\(-\tfrac{16}{375}\). Chained through the gradient of §2, \(d\varepsilon_1/dA_{G_1G_2}=\tfrac{10}{3}\): a 1-point error in the graders' agreement rate moves \(\hat\varepsilon_1\) by 3.3 points.

Falsifiers of the pipeline: \(G_1\) and \(G_2\) share a rubric or source (conditional independence fails; the constraint check is the test, with no
power at \(\pi=\tfrac12\)); any rater at or below chance (not identified, or the sign convention falsified); the sample touched by the loop
(`measurement_ledger` reused; `calibration_valid` withholds). The tests in step (5) take the corrected counts as given: they are an estimate, not
a sample, so the sampling error of \(\hat\eta_1\) is not in their p-values; §6 gives that error exactly.

## 6. The sampling law of \(\hat\eta_1\)

On \(m\) items the label table is \(\mathrm{Multinomial}(m;p)\); \(\hat\kappa_{ij}=(2N_{ij}-m)/m\) from the agreement counts, \(\hat S=\hat\kappa_{12}\hat\kappa_{13}/\hat\kappa_{23}\),
\(\hat\eta_1=(1-\sqrt{\hat S})/2\), *defined* iff every \(\hat\kappa>0\) and \(\hat S\le1\). Per item \((I_{12},I_{13},I_{23})\) takes four values only — all agree, or exactly
one pair — with probabilities \(q_{\text{all}}=p(000)+p(111)=\tfrac14(1+\sum\kappa)\) and \(q_{ij}=A_{ij}-q_{\text{all}}\), functions of the \(\kappa\)'s alone: **the law of
\(\hat\eta_1\) is free of the prior** and is the image of a four-category multinomial, enumerated in \(\binom{m+3}{3}\) integer terms (`sampling_law`: weights
over a common denominator \(D^m\), the square's class by integer comparison, its moments grouped by \(\hat\kappa_{23}\), the moments of \(\hat\eta_1\) bracketed
through \(\lfloor2^{16}\sqrt{\hat S}\rfloor\) per outcome). Enumerating all \(\binom{m+7}{7}\) label tables instead (`sampling_law_by_tables`; 245,157 at \(m=16\), 0.7 s)
gives every class probability and moment identically; the reduction reaches \(m=742\) in the receipt (68,638,340 terms; the whole receipt run, with
\(m=400\) too, takes about 7 minutes, almost all of it there). Moments are conditional on the defined event; "within" is
\(\Pr[\text{defined},\ |\hat\eta_1-\eta_1|\le\tfrac1{50}]\). Truth: \(S=\tfrac{16}{25}\), \(\eta_1=\tfrac1{10}\), \(d=(\tfrac45,\tfrac35,\tfrac35)\).

## 7. The asymmetric model (two-class Dawid–Skene)

Rater \(i\): false-negative \(\alpha_i=\Pr[X_i=0\mid Y=1]\), false-positive \(\beta_i=\Pr[X_i=1\mid Y=0]\); with \(\pi\), seven parameters on seven degrees of freedom
(`dawid_skene_model`). Write \(s_i=1-\alpha_i\), \(t_i=\beta_i\), \(\delta_i=1-\alpha_i-\beta_i\), \(u=\pi(1-\pi)\); from the table \(p_i=\Pr[X_i=1]\), \(c_{ij}=p_{ij}-p_ip_j\),
\(k_3=E\prod(X_i-p_i)=p_{123}-\sum_ip_ip_{jk}+2p_1p_2p_3\).

**Proposition 4.** \(c_{ij}=u\delta_i\delta_j\), \(k_3=u(1-2\pi)\delta_1\delta_2\delta_3\), so \(R^2:=k_3^2+4c_{12}c_{13}c_{23}=u^2\delta_1^2\delta_2^2\delta_3^2\) and, under \(\delta_1\delta_2\delta_3>0\), with \(\{i,j,k\}=\{1,2,3\}\):
\[\pi=\frac{R-k_3}{2R},\qquad s_i=p_i+\frac{R+k_3}{2c_{jk}},\qquad t_i=p_i-\frac{R-k_3}{2c_{jk}}.\]
*Proof.* \(s_i-p_i=(1-\pi)\delta_i\) and \(t_i-p_i=-\pi\delta_i\) have product \(-u\delta_i^2=-c_{ij}c_{ik}/c_{jk}\) and sum \((1-2\pi)\delta_i=k_3/c_{jk}\): the roots of
\(z^2-(k_3/c_{jk})z-c_{ij}c_{ik}/c_{jk}\), discriminant \(R^2/c_{jk}^2\); and \(u=c_{12}c_{13}c_{23}/R^2\) gives \(1-2\pi=k_3/R\). \(\square\) One root for everything: \(\pi\) is monotone
and each rate affine in \(R\), so a \(2^{-16}\) bracket on \(R\) brackets all seven (`dawid_skene_three_raters`; exact when \(R^2\) is a rational square, always at
expected counts since \(R=u|\delta_1\delta_2\delta_3|\)). Identifiable iff every \(c_{ij}\ne0\) (\(0<\pi<1\), every \(\delta_i\ne0\)) and \(R^2>0\). **Label switching:** \((\pi,\alpha,\beta)\)
and \((1-\pi,1-\beta,1-\alpha)\) give the same table (\(\delta\mapsto-\delta\)); `all_informative` (\(\delta_i>0\): hit rate above false-alarm rate for every rater) needs every
\(c_{ij}>0\) and refuses otherwise; `rater_1_informative` fixes \(\delta_1>0\), puts \(\sigma=\mathrm{sign}\,c_{23}\) in the formulas and recovers an anti-informative \(G_2\)
exactly (\((\alpha_2,\beta_2)=(\tfrac35,\tfrac35)\), \(\delta_2=-\tfrac15\)). Both solutions are returned.

**Fixture.** \(\pi=\tfrac14\), \(\alpha=(\tfrac1{10},\tfrac15,\tfrac1{10})\), \(\beta=(\tfrac15,\tfrac1{10},\tfrac3{10})\) (gold misses 10% of positives, false-alarms on 20% of negatives; the
controller is right on 90% / 70%): \(\delta=(\tfrac7{10},\tfrac7{10},\tfrac35)\), \(c=(\tfrac{147}{1600},\tfrac{63}{800},\tfrac{63}{800})\), \(k_3=\tfrac{441}{16000}\), \(R=\tfrac{441}{8000}\), every parameter exact; so on a
grid of 256 points, and on the symmetric grid the fit returns \(\alpha_i=\beta_i=e_i\), the \(\eta\)'s of §2. The exact Jacobian of \((\pi,\alpha,\beta)\mapsto\) cells (affine in
each parameter, so differences are exact) has rank 7 there and on the symmetric grid (5 with a chance rater): **no degree of freedom is left, no
equality constraint, hence no test of conditional independence** — against the symmetric model's three. Only inequalities remain:
\(p(100)=p(010)=p(001)=\tfrac7{30}\), \(p(011)=p(101)=p(110)=\tfrac1{10}\) has \(R^2=-\tfrac{49}{30000}\), no real point (`outside_model`); and rates must lie in \([0,1]\). The copy
grader of §5 passes both: at \(\rho=1\) the fit is exact and in range — \(\pi=\tfrac3{10}\), \(\alpha_1=\beta_1=\alpha_2=\beta_2=0\), controller \((\tfrac7{20},\tfrac{31}{140})\): two *perfect*
graders and an asymmetric controller — while the symmetric constraints fail; \(\rho=\tfrac12\) likewise (bracketed). The dependence §3 detects is
absorbed as asymmetry. A fixture table with \(\tfrac1{100}\) moved between two cells is bracketed and in range.

**Asymmetric inversion** (`asymmetric_gold_noise_inverse`, `calibrate_asymmetric`). With \(a_y\) the controller's accuracy on class \(y\) (\(1-\alpha_3\), \(1-\beta_3\)),
\(f_y\) the gold flip rate (\(\alpha_1\), \(\beta_1\)), the judge depending on correctness only, measured against \(G_1\): \(a'=\sum_y\pi_y(a_y(1-f_y)+(1-a_y)f_y)\),
\(\varepsilon'=\sum_y\pi_y(f_y+(1-2f_y)(a_y\varepsilon_0+(1-a_y)\varepsilon_1))\), \(w=\sum_y\pi_y((1-a_y)(1-f_y)\varepsilon_1+a_yf_y(1-\varepsilon_0))\). The agreement rate \(\Pr[C=J]\) **is still invariant**:
\(C\oplus F=J\oplus F\) iff \(C=J\), whatever the law of \(F\). Given the fit, \(\varepsilon'\) and \(w\) are affine in \((\varepsilon_0,\varepsilon_1)\): with \(F=\sum\pi_yf_y\), \(E_a=\sum\pi_y(1-2f_y)a_y\),
\(E_b=\sum\pi_y(1-2f_y)(1-a_y)\), \(G_a=\sum\pi_ya_yf_y\), \(G_b=\sum\pi_y(1-a_y)(1-f_y)\), \(\Delta=E_aG_b+E_bG_a\):
\[\varepsilon_1=\frac{E_a(w-G_a)+G_a(\varepsilon'-F)}{\Delta},\qquad\varepsilon_0=\frac{G_b(\varepsilon'-F)-E_b(w-G_a)}{\Delta},\]
\(a=\pi a_1+(1-\pi)a_0\), \(\varepsilon=a\varepsilon_0+(1-a)\varepsilon_1\); \(a'\) is reproduced identically. Symmetric case: \(\Delta=a(1-a)(1-2\eta)\) and the judge note's inversion (checked
on a grid). Record fixture, \(m=4000\) (label table integral; \(a=\tfrac34\), \(\varepsilon=\tfrac1{10}\), judges \(\varepsilon_1=\tfrac1{10}\) and the ceiling \(\tfrac25\)): measured \(a'=\tfrac{67}{100}\),
\(\varepsilon'=\tfrac6{25}\), \(w=\tfrac{27}{200}\) and \(\varepsilon'=\tfrac{237}{1000}\), \(w=\tfrac{417}{2000}\); both judges recovered exactly, corrected \((2700,300,900,100)\) (\(p=0.515\), Fisher 0.521) and
\((3000,0,600,400)\) (\(p<10^{-136}\)). The **symmetric pipeline on the same records** fails its constraints (residuals \((\tfrac{21}{500},\tfrac{21}{200},0)\)), brackets
\(\hat\eta_1\approx0.1634\) (the marginal flip rate is \(\tfrac7{40}\)), inverts to \(\hat\varepsilon_1\approx0.124\) and \(0.418\); the symmetric inversion at the marginal flip rate gives
\(\tfrac5{62}\approx0.081\) and \(\tfrac{239}{620}\approx0.385\): asymmetric gold is misread in both directions, and the constraint check flags it. *Evidence status.*
Proposition 4, the covariance, delta and inversion formulas: *algebraic identity*, enumeration-checked; the laws, fixtures and falsifiers: *finite verified examples*.

## 8. Not delivered

- No observed graders; binary labels only. On real counts the squares and \(R^2\) are not perfect squares: brackets.
- The sampling law is conditional on the defined event; the moments of \(\hat\eta_1\) are brackets, not rationals; no joint interval for
  \((\hat\eta_1,\hat\varepsilon_1)\); the only exact confidence statement is the one-sided disagreement bound, which ignores the controller. No sampling law
  for the Dawid–Skene fit.
- A bracketed Dawid–Skene fit is inverted at both ends of the bracket on \(R\); that brackets \(\hat\varepsilon_1\) only if the inversion is monotone in \(R\), not
  checked. The asymmetric model cannot test conditional independence (a fourth rater or the symmetric restriction is needed), and the symmetric
  check has no power at \(\pi=\tfrac12\).

66	+class FourRaterTable:
67	+    """Rational weights on the 2^4 cells ``(x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4)`` of four binary
68	+    raters' labels: the gold grader G1, a second grader G2, a third grader G3
69	+    and the controller's answer C.  One more independent grading of the same
70	+    sealed sample than ``LabelTable``: that is what a fourth rater costs."""

111	+def four_rater_model(prior, false_negatives, false_positives) -> FourRaterTable:
112	+    """Four conditionally independent raters with asymmetric rates: nine
113	+    parameters ``(pi, alpha_i, beta_i)`` on the fifteen degrees of freedom of
114	+    the 2^4 table, so six constraints (``four_rater_constraints``)."""
115	+
116	+    prior = _probability(prior, "prior")
117	+    alphas, betas = _four(false_negatives, "false_negatives"), _four(false_positives, "false_positives")
118	+    return FourRaterTable(_four_cells(prior, tuple(1 - a for a in alphas), betas))

121	+def four_rater_moments(table: FourRaterTable) -> dict[str, object]:
122	+    """Centred moments ``k_S = E prod_{i in S} (X_i - p_i)`` for every subset
123	+    with at least two raters, plus the marginals ``p_i``.  Under the model,
124	+    with ``u = pi (1 - pi)``, ``delta_i = 1 - alpha_i - beta_i`` and
125	+    ``E[X_i - p_i | Y] = delta_i (Y - pi)``: conditional independence gives
126	+    ``k_S = E[(Y - pi)^|S|] prod_{i in S} delta_i`` with ``E[(Y - pi)^2] = u``,
127	+    ``E[(Y - pi)^3] = u (1 - 2 pi)``, ``E[(Y - pi)^4] = u (1 - 3u)``.  So
128	+    ``c_ij = u delta_i delta_j``, ``k_ijk = u (1 - 2 pi) delta_i delta_j
129	+    delta_k`` and ``k_1234 = u (1 - 3u) delta_1 delta_2 delta_3 delta_4``."""
130	+
131	+    p = {i: sum((table.probability(c) for c in CELLS4 if c[i - 1] == 1), Q(0)) for i in range(1, 5)}
132	+    moments = {}
133	+    for subset in MOMENT_KEYS4[4:]:
134	+        total = Q(0)
135	+        for cell in CELLS4:
136	+            w = table.probability(cell)
137	+            for i in subset:
138	+                w *= cell[i - 1] - p[i]
139	+            total += w
140	+        moments[subset] = total
141	+    return {"marginals": p, "covariances": {pair: moments[pair] for pair in PAIRS4},
142	+            "third_moments": {t: moments[t] for t in TRIPLES4}, "fourth_moment": moments[(1, 2, 3, 4)]}

145	+def four_rater_residuals(moments: dict) -> dict[str, Q]:
146	+    """The six polynomial equalities, as residuals that vanish under the model.
147	+
148	+    Tetrads: ``c_12 c_34 = c_13 c_24 = c_14 c_23`` (each is ``u^2 prod delta``;
149	+    two independent equalities).  Third-moment ratios: ``k_ijk / k_ijl = c_ik
150	+    / c_il = delta_k / delta_l``; written without division, ``k_ijk c_il = k_ijl
151	+    c_ik`` (both are ``u^2 (1 - 2 pi) delta_i^2 delta_j delta_k delta_l``).  Six
152	+    such ratios exist, one per shared pair; given the tetrads three are
153	+    independent, the ones expressing ``k_124, k_134, k_234`` through ``k_123``.
154	+    Fourth moment: ``(k_1234 - c_12 c_34) c_12 = k_123 k_124``, since
155	+    ``k_1234 - c_12 c_34 = u (1 - 4u) prod delta = u (1 - 2 pi)^2 prod delta``
156	+    and ``k_123 k_124 = u^2 (1 - 2 pi)^2 delta_1^2 delta_2^2 delta_3 delta_4``.
157	+    The six have a rank-6 Jacobian in the moments (``constraint_jacobian_rank``)
158	+    and the model's parameter Jacobian has rank 9 on 15 degrees of freedom
159	+    (``four_rater_jacobian_rank``): exactly six independent equalities."""
160	+
161	+    c, k, m4 = moments["covariances"], moments["third_moments"], moments["fourth_moment"]
162	+    return {"tetrad_12_34_vs_13_24": c[(1, 2)] * c[(3, 4)] - c[(1, 3)] * c[(2, 4)],
163	+            "tetrad_13_24_vs_14_23": c[(1, 3)] * c[(2, 4)] - c[(1, 4)] * c[(2, 3)],
164	+            "third_123_vs_124": k[(1, 2, 3)] * c[(1, 4)] - k[(1, 2, 4)] * c[(1, 3)],
165	+            "third_123_vs_134": k[(1, 2, 3)] * c[(1, 4)] - k[(1, 3, 4)] * c[(1, 2)],
166	+            "third_123_vs_234": k[(1, 2, 3)] * c[(2, 4)] - k[(2, 3, 4)] * c[(1, 2)],
167	+            "fourth_moment": (m4 - c[(1, 2)] * c[(3, 4)]) * c[(1, 2)] - k[(1, 2, 3)] * k[(1, 2, 4)]}

170	+def constraint_jacobian_rank(moments: dict) -> int:
171	+    """Rank of the 6 x 15 Jacobian of the residuals in the centred moments
172	+    ``(p_i, c_ij, k_ijk, k_1234)``, which are a coordinate system on the
173	+    simplex.  Every residual has degree at most two in each single moment, so
174	+    the central difference ``(r(x + h) - r(x - h)) / 2h`` is the exact partial."""
175	+
176	+    flat = {(i,): moments["marginals"][i] for i in range(1, 5)}
177	+    flat.update(moments["covariances"])
178	+    flat.update(moments["third_moments"])
179	+    flat[(1, 2, 3, 4)] = moments["fourth_moment"]
180	+
181	+    def residuals_at(values: dict) -> list[Q]:
182	+        split = {"marginals": {i: values[(i,)] for i in range(1, 5)},
183	+                 "covariances": {pair: values[pair] for pair in PAIRS4},
184	+                 "third_moments": {t: values[t] for t in TRIPLES4}, "fourth_moment": values[(1, 2, 3, 4)]}
185	+        r = four_rater_residuals(split)
186	+        return [r[name] for name in CONSTRAINTS4]
187	+
188	+    h = Q(1)
189	+    columns = []
190	+    for key in MOMENT_KEYS4:
191	+        up, down = dict(flat), dict(flat)
192	+        up[key] += h
193	+        down[key] -= h
194	+        columns.append([(a - b) / (2 * h) for a, b in zip(residuals_at(up), residuals_at(down))])
195	+    return _rank([[col[r] for col in columns] for r in range(len(CONSTRAINTS4))])
196	+

198	+def four_rater_jacobian_rank(prior, false_negatives, false_positives) -> int:
199	+    """Rank of the exact 16 x 9 Jacobian of ``(pi, alpha, beta) -> cells``
200	+    (affine in each parameter, so one difference per column is exact): nine
201	+    wherever ``0 < pi < 1`` and every ``delta_i != 0``."""
202	+
203	+    prior = _probability(prior, "prior")
204	+    alphas, betas = _four(false_negatives, "false_negatives"), _four(false_positives, "false_positives")
205	+    sens = tuple(1 - a for a in alphas)
206	+    base = _four_cells(prior, sens, betas)
207	+
208	+    def column(moved_prior, moved_sens, moved_betas) -> list[Q]:
209	+        cells = _four_cells(moved_prior, moved_sens, moved_betas)
210	+        return [cells[c] - base[c] for c in CELLS4]
211	+
212	+    columns = [column(prior + 1, sens, betas)]
213	+    for i in range(4):
214	+        bumped = list(sens)
215	+        bumped[i] += 1
216	+        columns.append(column(prior, tuple(bumped), betas))
217	+        bumped = list(betas)
218	+        bumped[i] += 1
219	+        columns.append(column(prior, sens, tuple(bumped)))
220	+    return _rank([[col[r] for col in columns] for r in range(16)])

223	+def _merge_point(values: list) -> tuple[object, bool]:
224	+    """Exact values agree, or brackets intersect (returning the intersection)."""
225	+
226	+    if all(not isinstance(v, tuple) for v in values):
227	+        return values[0], all(v == values[0] for v in values)
228	+    lows = [v[0] if isinstance(v, tuple) else v for v in values]
229	+    highs = [v[1] if isinstance(v, tuple) else v for v in values]
230	+    low, high = max(lows), min(highs)
231	+    return (low, high), low <= high

234	+def dawid_skene_four_raters(table: FourRaterTable, convention: str = "all_informative",
235	+                            bits: int = ROOT_BITS) -> dict[str, object]:
236	+    """Fit the three-rater solution on each of the four triples and check that
237	+    they agree: the prior on all four, each rater's two rates on the three
238	+    triples containing it.  Statuses: a triple's failure status
239	+    (``not_identified``, ``outside_model``, ``convention_violated``), ``exact``
240	+    (all triples exact and equal), ``bracketed`` (every bracket intersects;
241	+    the solution is the intersection) or ``inconsistent``.  Agreement uses
242	+    moments of order at most three; the fourth-moment constraint is checked
243	+    separately by ``four_rater_constraints``."""
244	+
245	+    fits = {}
246	+    for triple in TRIPLES4:
247	+        (drop,) = set(range(1, 5)) - set(triple)
248	+        fits[triple] = dawid_skene_three_raters(table.triple(drop), convention, bits)
249	+    out = {"convention": convention, "triple_fits": fits,
250	+           "degrees_of_freedom_left": DEGREES_OF_FREEDOM["four_rater_free_cell_probabilities"]
251	+           - DEGREES_OF_FREEDOM["four_rater_parameters"]}
252	+    bad = [f["status"] for f in fits.values() if f["status"] not in ("exact", "bracketed")]
253	+    if bad:
254	+        out["status"] = bad[0]
255	+        return out
256	+    prior, ok = _merge_point([f["solution"]["prior"] for f in fits.values()])
257	+    solution = {"prior": prior, "false_negatives": {}, "false_positives": {}, "deltas": {}}
258	+    for i in range(1, 5):
259	+        for key in ("false_negatives", "false_positives", "deltas"):
260	+            values = [f["solution"][key][triple.index(i) + 1] for triple, f in fits.items() if i in triple]
261	+            merged, agree = _merge_point(values)
262	+            solution[key][i] = merged
263	+            ok = ok and agree
264	+    exact = all(f["status"] == "exact" for f in fits.values())
265	+    out.update({"status": "inconsistent" if not ok else "exact" if exact else "bracketed",
266	+                "solution": solution, "triples_agree": ok})
267	+    if ok:
268	+        flat = [solution["prior"]] + list(solution["false_negatives"].values()) + list(solution["false_positives"].values())
269	+        out["in_range"] = all((0 <= v <= 1) if not isinstance(v, tuple) else (0 <= v[0] and v[1] <= 1) for v in flat)
270	+    return out

273	+def four_rater_constraints(table: FourRaterTable, convention: str = "all_informative",
274	+                           bits: int = ROOT_BITS) -> dict[str, object]:
275	+    """The exact test: a table is the image of a four-rater model with every
276	+    ``c_ij != 0`` iff the six residuals vanish, the triple fits agree and the
277	+    implied nine parameters lie in ``[0, 1]``.  Proof of the converse: the
278	+    fifteen centred moments determine the table; the triple-(1,2,3) fit
279	+    matches ``p_1, p_2, p_3, c_12, c_13, c_23, k_123``; ``delta_4 = c_14 / (u
280	+    delta_1)`` and ``p_4`` fix rater 4; the tetrads then give ``c_24, c_34``,
281	+    the three ratio equalities ``k_124, k_134, k_234`` and the fourth-moment
282	+    equality ``k_1234``.  When the fit is exact the reconstruction is run and
283	+    compared cell by cell (``reproduces_table``)."""
284	+
285	+    moments = four_rater_moments(table)
286	+    residuals = four_rater_residuals(moments)
287	+    cov = moments["covariances"]
288	+    identifiable = all(c != 0 for c in cov.values())
289	+    equalities = all(r == 0 for r in residuals.values())
290	+    fit = dawid_skene_four_raters(table, convention, bits)
291	+    in_range = fit.get("in_range")
292	+    reproduces = None
293	+    if fit["status"] == "exact" and in_range:
294	+        s = fit["solution"]
295	+        rebuilt = four_rater_model(s["prior"], tuple(s["false_negatives"][i] for i in range(1, 5)),
296	+                                   tuple(s["false_positives"][i] for i in range(1, 5)))
297	+        reproduces = all(rebuilt.cells[c] * table.total == table.cells[c] for c in CELLS4)
298	+    passes = (equalities and identifiable and fit["status"] in ("exact", "bracketed") and bool(in_range)
299	+              and reproduces is not False)
300	+    return {"moments": moments, "residuals": residuals, "equalities_hold": equalities,
301	+            "identifiable": identifiable, "fit": fit, "in_range": in_range,
302	+            "reproduces_table": reproduces, "passes": passes,
303	+            "constraint_count": len(CONSTRAINTS4)}

306	+def copy_grader_table4(prior, false_negatives, false_positives, copy_rate) -> FourRaterTable:
307	+    """Four raters where G2 copies G1 with probability ``rho`` and otherwise
308	+    labels independently at its own rates.  Given ``Y``, ``X_2`` stays
309	+    independent of ``X_3, X_4``, with effective rates ``rho (alpha_1, beta_1) +
310	+    (1 - rho)(alpha_2, beta_2)``; only the pair (1, 2) is dependent."""
311	+
312	+    prior, rho = _probability(prior, "prior"), _probability(copy_rate, "copy_rate")
313	+    alphas, betas = _four(false_negatives, "false_negatives"), _four(false_positives, "false_positives")
314	+    sens = tuple(1 - a for a in alphas)
315	+    cells = {}
316	+    for cell in CELLS4:
317	+        weight = Q(0)
318	+        for y in (0, 1):
319	+            w = prior if y else 1 - prior
320	+            for i in (0, 2, 3):
321	+                hit = sens[i] if y else betas[i]
322	+                w *= hit if cell[i] == 1 else 1 - hit
323	+            own = sens[1] if y else betas[1]
324	+            w *= rho * (1 if cell[1] == cell[0] else 0) + (1 - rho) * (own if cell[1] == 1 else 1 - own)
325	+            weight += w
326	+        cells[cell] = weight
327	+    return FourRaterTable(cells)

330	+def copy_grader_tetrad_residual(prior, false_negatives, false_positives, copy_rate) -> Q:
331	+    """Closed form of the tetrad residual ``c_12 c_34 - c_13 c_24`` (and of
332	+    ``c_12 c_34 - c_14 c_23``) under copying: ``rho V_1 c_34`` with ``V_1 =
333	+    pi alpha_1 (1 - alpha_1) + (1 - pi) beta_1 (1 - beta_1)`` (the mean
334	+    conditional variance of G1's label) and ``c_34 = u delta_3 delta_4``.
335	+    Proof: ``E[X_1 X_2 | Y] = rho E[X_1 | Y] + (1 - rho) E[X_1 | Y] E[X_2' | Y]``
336	+    exceeds the conditionally independent value ``E[X_1 | Y] E[X_2 | Y]`` by
337	+    ``rho Var(X_1 | Y)``, so ``c_12 = u delta_1 delta_2~ + rho V_1`` while
338	+    ``c_13, c_24, c_34`` keep their product form; the tetrad ``c_13 c_24 -
339	+    c_14 c_23`` is unaffected.  Any ``rho > 0`` is detected whenever G1 is
340	+    imperfect, ``0 < pi < 1`` and raters 3 and 4 are informative: the failing
341	+    tetrads name the dependent pair."""
342	+
343	+    prior, rho = _probability(prior, "prior"), _probability(copy_rate, "copy_rate")
344	+    alphas, betas = _four(false_negatives, "false_negatives"), _four(false_positives, "false_positives")
345	+    u = prior * (1 - prior)
346	+    v1 = prior * alphas[0] * (1 - alphas[0]) + (1 - prior) * betas[0] * (1 - betas[0])
347	+    c34 = u * (1 - alphas[2] - betas[2]) * (1 - alphas[3] - betas[3])
348	+    return rho * v1 * c34

369	+    the class ``"sign"`` (some ``kappa_hat <= 0``) or ``"range"`` (``S_hat > 1``)."""

384	+def _threshold(rest: int, sigma: int, rhs: int, den: int, strict: bool) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
385	+    """The ``k_12`` tails where ``a b <= C`` (or ``< C``), as ``(K_lo, K_hi)``:
386	+    ``k_12 <= K_lo`` or ``k_12 >= K_hi``; ``None`` when every ``k_12`` qualifies.
387	+    With ``a + b = sigma`` and ``a - b = 4 k_12 - 2 rest``: ``a b = (sigma^2 -
388	+    (a - b)^2) / 4 <= C`` iff ``den (a - b)^2 >= den sigma^2 - 4 den C = rhs``."""
389	+
390	+    if rhs < 0 or (rhs == 0 and not strict):
391	+        return None
392	+    y = rhs // den + 1 if strict else (rhs + den - 1) // den
393	+    q = isqrt(y - 1) + 1
394	+    return (2 * rest - q) // 4, -((-(2 * rest + q)) // 4)

397	+def square_tail_law(size, errors, observed, thresholds=()) -> dict[str, object]:
398	+    """Exact tails of the extended square ``S~`` under the four-pattern
399	+    multinomial, in ``O(m^2)`` big-integer products instead of the ``C(m+3, 3)``
400	+    terms of ``sampling_law``.  ``S~`` orders sign failures (some ``kappa_hat <=

522	+def eta_confidence_set(size, counts, eta2, accuracy, alpha, grid, use_square_test: bool = True,
523	+                       resolution=RESOLUTION, workers: int = 1) -> dict[str, object]:
524	+    """Step 1 of the joint statement: the grid points ``eta_0`` not rejected
525	+    by (a) the one-sided disagreement bound (``eta_0 <= 1 - A_L`` from
526	+    ``N_12`` alone; no plug-in) and, when asked, (b) the exact two-sided test
527	+    of the observed ``S_hat`` under ``eta_1 = eta_0`` with ``(eta_2, a)`` at
528	+    the plug-in values.  Each test runs at level ``alpha / 2`` when both are
529	+    used (``alpha`` when only (a) is), so the intersection has confidence at
530	+    least ``1 - alpha`` under the plug-in."""
531	+
532	+    m, alpha = _size(size), _probability(alpha, "alpha")
533	+    if not 0 < alpha < 1:
534	+        raise ValueError("alpha must lie strictly inside (0, 1)")
535	+    eta2, accuracy = _probability(eta2, "eta2"), _probability(accuracy, "accuracy")
536	+    points = sorted({_probability(e, "grid point") for e in grid})
537	+    if not points or any(e >= HALF for e in points):
538	+        raise ValueError("grid must be a nonempty list of rationals in [0, 1/2)")
539	+    level = alpha / 2 if use_square_test else alpha
540	+    bound = disagreement_bound(m, counts[(1, 2)], level, resolution)
541	+    observed = observed_square(m, counts)
542	+    rows = [{"eta0": eta0, "passes_disagreement_bound": eta0 <= bound["eta_upper_bound"], "square_p": None}
543	+            for eta0 in points]
544	+    for row in rows:
545	+        row["retained"] = row["passes_disagreement_bound"]
546	+    if use_square_test:
547	+        todo = [row for row in rows if row["retained"]]
548	+        jobs = [(m, (row["eta0"], eta2, 1 - accuracy), observed) for row in todo]
549	+        if workers > 1 and len(jobs) > 1:
550	+            from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor
551	+            with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=min(workers, len(jobs))) as pool:
552	+                values = list(pool.map(_square_p, jobs))
553	+        else:
554	+            values = [_square_p(job) for job in jobs]
555	+        for row, p in zip(todo, values):
556	+            row["square_p"] = p
557	+            row["retained"] = p >= level
558	+    retained = [r["eta0"] for r in rows if r["retained"]]
559	+    return {"size": m, "counts": counts, "observed_square": observed, "alpha": alpha, "level_per_test": level,
560	+            "tests_used": ("disagreement_bound", "square_test") if use_square_test else ("disagreement_bound",),
561	+            "plug_in": {"eta2": eta2, "accuracy": accuracy}, "disagreement_bound": bound, "rows": rows,
562	+            "retained": retained, "grid": points}

570	+    """The judge note's inversion at ``eta`` with every rate clamped into its
571	+    feasible range: ``a`` and ``eps`` into ``[0, 1]``, ``eps_1`` into the
572	+    ``shared_error_bounds`` at the clamped ``(a, eps)``.  An ``eta`` with ``eta
573	+    >= 1 - a'`` implies a perfect controller (no wrong items) and returns
574	+    ``None``.  A clamp means the observed judge table is not the image of any

601	+    counts rounded half-up, the exact ceiling and independence tests and the
602	+    two-sided level-``alpha`` Clopper-Pearson bracket for ``eps_1``; (3) with

634	+    out.update({"agreement_counts": counts, "plug_in_bracketed": eta2_bracketed or accuracy_bracketed,

636	+    if measured["table"] is None:

171	
172	    In Walsh coordinates, with ``tau = 1 - 2 prior`` and ``d_i = 1 - 2 e_i``:
173	    ``p_S = tau^[|S| odd] prod_{i in S} d_i``.  Proof: ``E[(-1)^{X_i} | Y] =
174	    (-1)^Y d_i``, the raters are independent given ``Y``, and ``E[(-1)^{kY}]``
175	    is ``tau`` for odd ``k`` and ``1`` for even ``k``."""
176	
177	    prior = _probability(prior, "prior")
178	    if not isinstance(errors, (tuple, list)) or len(errors) != 3:
179	        raise ValueError("errors must list three rates")
180	    errors = tuple(_probability(e, f"error of rater {i + 1}") for i, e in enumerate(errors))
181	    cells = {}
182	    for cell in CELLS3:
183	        weight = Q(0)
184	        for y in (0, 1):
185	            w = prior if y else 1 - prior
186	            for i in range(3):
187	                w *= (1 - errors[i]) if cell[i] == y else errors[i]
188	            weight += w
189	        cells[cell] = weight
190	    return LabelTable(cells)
191

193	# --- identification from the pairwise polarities -----------------------------
194	
195	def polarity_squares(kappas: dict[tuple[int, int], Q]) -> dict[int, Q]:
196	    """``(1 - 2 e_i)^2 = kappa_ij kappa_ik / kappa_jk``.
197	
198	    Proof: ``kappa_ij = d_i d_j`` for conditionally independent symmetric
199	    raters, so the ratio is ``d_i d_j d_i d_k / (d_j d_k) = d_i^2``.  A rater
200	    at chance has ``d = 0``, both of its polarities vanish, and the other two
201	    raters are left unidentified (one equation, two unknowns)."""
202	
203	    values = {pair: _as_q(kappas[pair], f"kappa {pair}") for pair in PAIRS}
204	    if any(k == 0 for k in values.values()):
205	        raise ValueError("a rater at chance (kappa = 0) leaves the others unidentified")
206	    return {i: values[_pair(i, j)] * values[_pair(i, k)] / values[_pair(j, k)]
207	            for i in (1, 2, 3) for j, k in (_others(i),)}
208	
209	
210	def exact_square_root(value) -> Q | None:
211	    """The rational square root of ``value`` if it has one, else ``None``.  A
212	    fraction in lowest terms is a rational square iff numerator and
213	    denominator are both perfect squares."""
214	
215	    value = _as_q(value, "value")
216	    if value < 0:
217	        return None
218	    n, d = isqrt(value.numerator), isqrt(value.denominator)
219	    return Q(n, d) if n * n == value.numerator and d * d == value.denominator else None
220	
221	
222	def _square_in_range(square) -> Q:
223	    square = _as_q(square, "square")
224	    if not 0 <= square <= 1:
225	        raise ValueError("no error rate in [0, 1/2] has this squared polarity")
226	    return square
227	
228	
229	def error_rate_from_square(square) -> Q | None:
230	    """``e = (1 - sqrt(square)) / 2`` exactly when the square is a perfect
231	    square (always the case at expected counts with rational rates); ``None``
232	    otherwise.  The sign is fixed by ``e < 1/2``."""
233	
234	    root = exact_square_root(_square_in_range(square))
235	    return None if root is None else (1 - root) / 2
236	
237	
238	def error_rate_at_most(square, bound) -> bool:
239	    """Exact membership ``e <= bound`` for rational ``bound`` without taking the
240	    root: ``e <= bound`` iff ``d >= 1 - 2 bound`` iff (for ``1 - 2 bound > 0``)
241	    ``square >= (1 - 2 bound)^2``; trivially true when ``bound >= 1/2``."""
242	
243	    square, bound = _square_in_range(square), _probability(bound, "bound")
244	    floor = 1 - 2 * bound
245	    return True if floor <= 0 else square >= floor * floor
246	
247	
248	def error_rate_bracket(square, resolution=RESOLUTION) -> dict[str, object]:
249	    """Rational bracket of width at most ``resolution`` around ``e``, by
250	    bisection on the exact membership test; exact when the square is perfect.
251	    The true ``e`` lies in ``(lower, upper]``."""
252	
253	    square, resolution = _square_in_range(square), _as_q(resolution, "resolution")
254	    if resolution <= 0:
255	        raise ValueError("resolution must be positive")
256	    exact = error_rate_from_square(square)
257	    if exact is not None:
258	        return {"lower": exact, "upper": exact, "exact": exact, "width": Q(0), "resolution": resolution}
259	    low, high = Q(0), HALF
260	    while high - low > resolution:
261	        mid = (low + high) / 2
262	        if error_rate_at_most(square, mid):
263	            high = mid
264	        else:
265	            low = mid
266	    return {"lower": low, "upper": high, "exact": None, "width": high - low, "resolution": resolution}
267	
268	
269	def eta_gradient(kappas: dict[tuple[int, int], Q], rater: int = 1) -> dict[str, object] | None:
270	    """Partial derivatives of ``e_i = (1 - sqrt(kappa_ij kappa_ik / kappa_jk)) / 2``:
271	    ``-d_i / (4 kappa_ij)``, ``-d_i / (4 kappa_ik)``, ``+d_i / (4 kappa_jk)``;
272	    exact only when ``d_i`` is rational, else ``None``.  Per agreement rate the
273	    values double, since ``kappa = 2 A - 1``."""
274	
275	    if rater not in (1, 2, 3):
276	        raise ValueError("rater must be 1, 2 or 3")
277	    root = exact_square_root(polarity_squares(kappas)[rater])
278	    if root is None:
279	        return None
280	    j, k = _others(rater)
281	    per_kappa = {_pair(rater, j): -root / (4 * kappas[_pair(rater, j)]),
282	                 _pair(rater, k): -root / (4 * kappas[_pair(rater, k)]),
283	                 _pair(j, k): root / (4 * kappas[_pair(j, k)])}
284	    return {"polarity": root, "per_kappa": per_kappa,
285	            "per_agreement_rate": {pair: 2 * g for pair, g in per_kappa.items()}}
286

288	# --- 2. the model's testable constraints -------------------------------------
289	
290	def model_constraints(table: LabelTable) -> dict[str, object]:
291	    """Residuals of the three equalities ``M_i kappa_jk - P`` (each is
292	    ``tau d_i d_j d_k - tau d_1 d_2 d_3 = 0`` under the model), the sign
293	    condition (``kappa_ij = d_i d_j`` has zero or two negative pairs, never one
294	    or three), the range conditions (``d_i^2 <= 1`` and ``tau^2 = M_i^2 / d_i^2
295	    <= 1``) and identifiability (every ``kappa > 0`` under ``e_i < 1/2``).
296	
297	    At ``tau = 0`` (balanced prior) every odd coefficient vanishes and the
298	    equalities read ``0 = 0``: they then have no power against dependence."""
299	
300	    coefficients = walsh_coefficients(table)
301	    kappas = {pair: coefficients[pair] for pair in PAIRS}
302	    biases = {i: coefficients[(i,)] for i in (1, 2, 3)}
303	    parity = coefficients[(1, 2, 3)]
304	    residuals = {i: biases[i] * kappas[_others(i)] - parity for i in (1, 2, 3)}
305	    negatives = sum(1 for k in kappas.values() if k < 0)
306	    chance = any(k == 0 for k in kappas.values())
307	    squares = None if chance else polarity_squares(kappas)
308	    squares_ok = None if chance else all(0 <= s <= 1 for s in squares.values())
309	    prior_ok = None if chance else all(biases[i] ** 2 <= squares[i] for i in (1, 2, 3))
310	    equalities = all(r == 0 for r in residuals.values())
311	    signs = negatives in (0, 2)
312	    consistent = equalities and signs and squares_ok is not False and prior_ok is not False
313	    identifiable = negatives == 0 and not chance
314	    return {"kappas": kappas, "biases": biases, "parity": parity, "residuals": residuals,
315	            "equalities_hold": equalities, "negative_kappas": negatives, "signs_consistent": signs,
316	            "chance_rater": chance, "squares": squares, "squares_in_unit_interval": squares_ok,
317	            "prior_in_range": prior_ok, "model_consistent": consistent,
318	            "identifiable": identifiable, "passes": consistent and identifiable,
319	            "vacuous_at_balanced_prior": all(b == 0 for b in biases.values()) and parity == 0}
320	
321	
322	def _rank(rows: list[list[Q]]) -> int:
323	    matrix = [list(row) for row in rows]
324	    rank = 0
325	    for col in range(len(matrix[0]) if matrix else 0):
326	        pivot = next((r for r in range(rank, len(matrix)) if matrix[r][col] != 0), None)
327	        if pivot is None:
328	            continue
329	        matrix[rank], matrix[pivot] = matrix[pivot], matrix[rank]
330	        for r in range(len(matrix)):
331	            if r != rank and matrix[r][col] != 0:
332	                factor = matrix[r][col] / matrix[rank][col]
333	                matrix[r] = [x - factor * y for x, y in zip(matrix[r], matrix[rank])]
334	        rank += 1
335	    return rank
336	
337	
338	def model_jacobian_rank(prior, errors) -> int:
339	    """Rank of the exact Jacobian of ``(tau, d_1, d_2, d_3) -> (p_S)_S`` at the
340	    point: four wherever every ``d_i != 0`` (the three pair rows alone have
341	    determinant ``-2 d_1 d_2 d_3`` on the ``d`` columns), so the model is
342	    four-dimensional inside the seven-dimensional simplex and leaves exactly
343	    three constraints.  With a chance rater the rank drops at a balanced prior
344	    (``tau = 0``) but not at an unbalanced one, where the marginal bias
345	    ``tau d_i`` still moves."""
346	
347	    tau = 1 - 2 * _probability(prior, "prior")
348	    if not isinstance(errors, (tuple, list)) or len(errors) != 3:
349	        raise ValueError("errors must list three rates")
350	    d1, d2, d3 = (1 - 2 * _probability(e, "error") for e in errors)
351	    zero = Q(0)
352	    rows = [[d1, tau, zero, zero], [d2, zero, tau, zero], [d3, zero, zero, tau],
353	            [zero, d2, d1, zero], [zero, d3, zero, d1], [zero, zero, d3, d2],
354	            [d1 * d2 * d3, tau * d2 * d3, tau * d1 * d3, tau * d1 * d2]]
355	    return _rank(rows)
356	
357	
358	def copy_grader_table(prior, eta1, eta2, controller_error, copy_rate) -> LabelTable:
359	    """Labels when G2 copies G1 with probability ``copy_rate`` and otherwise
360	    grades independently at ``eta2``: conditional independence fails.  Closed
361	    form of the residuals: ``r_1 = r_2 = -tau d_C rho 4 eta1 (1 - eta1)``,
362	    ``r_3 = 0``; the failing constraints name the dependent pair."""
363	
364	    prior, rho = _probability(prior, "prior"), _probability(copy_rate, "copy_rate")
365	    eta1, eta2, ec = (_probability(eta1, "eta1"), _probability(eta2, "eta2"),
366	                      _probability(controller_error, "controller_error"))
367	    cells = {}
368	    for cell in CELLS3:
369	        g1, g2, c = cell
370	        weight = Q(0)
371	        for y in (0, 1):
372	            w = prior if y else 1 - prior
373	            w *= (1 - eta1) if g1 == y else eta1
374	            w *= rho * (1 if g2 == g1 else 0) + (1 - rho) * ((1 - eta2) if g2 == y else eta2)
375	            w *= (1 - ec) if c == y else ec
376	            weight += w
377	        cells[cell] = weight
378	    return LabelTable(cells)
379	
380	
381	def copy_grader_residual(prior, eta1, controller_error, copy_rate) -> Q:
382	    """``-tau d_C rho 4 eta1 (1 - eta1)``, the residual of constraints 1 and 2."""
383	
384	    tau = 1 - 2 * _probability(prior, "prior")
385	    d_c = 1 - 2 * _probability(controller_error, "controller_error")
386	    eta1, rho = _probability(eta1, "eta1"), _probability(copy_rate, "copy_rate")
387	    return -tau * d_c * rho * 4 * eta1 * (1 - eta1)

390	# --- 3. the record table and the pipeline ------------------------------------
391	
392	@dataclass(frozen=True)
393	class RecordTable:
394	    """Rational weights on the 2^4 cells ``(x_C, v_J, g_1, g_2)``: the
395	    controller's answer, the judge's verdict (``1`` = "correct"), the gold
396	    label and the second grader's label.  Counts on a sealed sample, or
397	    expected counts."""
398	
399	    cells: dict
400	
401	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
402	        object.__setattr__(self, "cells", _weights(self.cells, CELLS4, "(x_C, v_J, g_1, g_2) in {0,1}^4"))
403	
404	    @property
405	    def total(self) -> Q:
406	        return sum(self.cells.values(), Q(0))
407	
408	    def label_table(self) -> LabelTable:
409	        """Marginal over the judge: ``(g_1, g_2, x_C)`` as raters 1, 2, 3."""
410	
411	        cells = {cell: Q(0) for cell in CELLS3}
412	        for (x, _v, g1, g2), weight in self.cells.items():
413	            cells[(g1, g2, x)] += weight
414	        return LabelTable(cells)
415	
416	    def judge_cells(self, gold: int = 1) -> dict[str, Q]:
417	        """The judge note's 2x2 table measured against grader ``gold``:
418	        controller right iff ``x_C`` equals that label, judge right iff its
419	        verdict equals that measured correctness."""
420	
421	        if gold not in (1, 2):
422	            raise ValueError("gold must be 1 or 2")
423	        names = {(1, 1): "right_right", (1, 0): "right_wrong", (0, 1): "wrong_right", (0, 0): "wrong_wrong"}
424	        out = {name: Q(0) for name in names.values()}
425	        for (x, v, g1, g2), weight in self.cells.items():
426	            c = int(x == (g1 if gold == 1 else g2))
427	            out[names[(c, int(v == c))]] += weight
428	        return out

431	def expected_record_table(size: int, prior, accuracy, judge_error, eps1, eta1, eta2,
432	                          copy_rate=Q(0)) -> RecordTable:
433	    """Expected counts for ``size`` items: ``Y ~ Bernoulli(prior)``; the
434	    controller answers ``Y`` with probability ``a``; the judge says "correct"
435	    with probability ``1 - eps0`` on a right answer and ``eps1`` on a wrong
436	    one; G1 flips ``Y`` at ``eta1``; G2 copies G1 with probability
437	    ``copy_rate`` (zero for an independent grader) and otherwise flips at
438	    ``eta2``."""
439	
440	    if type(size) is not int or size < 1:
441	        raise ValueError("size must be a positive integer")
442	    prior, accuracy = _probability(prior, "prior"), _probability(accuracy, "accuracy")
443	    judge_error, eps1 = _probability(judge_error, "judge_error"), _probability(eps1, "eps1")
444	    eta1, eta2, rho = (_probability(eta1, "eta1"), _probability(eta2, "eta2"),
445	                       _probability(copy_rate, "copy_rate"))
446	    low, high = shared_error_bounds(accuracy, judge_error)
447	    if not low <= eps1 <= high:
448	        raise ValueError("eps1 is infeasible for the marginal judge error")
449	    eps0 = (judge_error - (1 - accuracy) * eps1) / accuracy
450	    cells = {}
451	    for cell in CELLS4:
452	        x, v, g1, g2 = cell
453	        weight = Q(0)
454	        for y in (0, 1):
455	            w = prior if y else 1 - prior
456	            right = x == y
457	            w *= accuracy if right else 1 - accuracy
458	            says_correct = (1 - eps0) if right else eps1
459	            w *= says_correct if v == 1 else 1 - says_correct
460	            w *= (1 - eta1) if g1 == y else eta1
461	            w *= rho * (1 if g2 == g1 else 0) + (1 - rho) * ((1 - eta2) if g2 == y else eta2)
462	            weight += w
463	        cells[cell] = size * weight
464	    return RecordTable(cells)
465	
466	
467	def measured_judge_rates(record: RecordTable, gold: int = 1) -> dict[str, object]:
468	    """``a'``, ``eps'``, ``w = W1'/m`` and ``eps1'`` of the table measured
469	    against grader ``gold``, plus the half-up rounded ``JudgeTable`` when the
470	    total is an integer count (``None`` for a probability table)."""
471	
472	    cells = record.judge_cells(gold)
473	    m = record.total
474	    measured_accuracy = (cells["right_right"] + cells["right_wrong"]) / m
475	    measured_error = (cells["right_wrong"] + cells["wrong_wrong"]) / m
476	    wrong_wrong_rate = cells["wrong_wrong"] / m
477	    table, changed = None, None
478	    if m.denominator == 1:
479	        try:
480	            table, changed = rounded_table(cells)
481	        except ValueError:  # every cell rounds to zero: no table to test
482	            pass
483	    return {"cells": cells, "accuracy": measured_accuracy, "judge_error": measured_error,
484	            "wrong_wrong_rate": wrong_wrong_rate,
485	            "eps1": None if measured_accuracy == 1 else wrong_wrong_rate / (1 - measured_accuracy),
486	            "table": table, "rounding_changed_a_cell": changed}
487	
488	
489	def inverted_eps1(measured_accuracy, measured_error, wrong_wrong_rate, eta) -> Q:
490	    """Proposition 2 inverted as one rational function of ``eta``:
491	    ``eps1(eta) = (w (1 - 2 eta) - eta (a' - eps')) / (1 - a' - eta)``.
492	    Proof: substitute ``a - eps = (a' - eps') / (1 - 2 eta)`` and
493	    ``1 - a = (1 - a' - eta) / (1 - 2 eta)`` into the note's
494	    ``eps1 = (eps1' (1 - a') - eta (a - eps)) / (1 - a)`` with
495	    ``eps1' (1 - a') = w``."""
496	
497	    a, e, w = (_probability(measured_accuracy, "measured_accuracy"),
498	               _probability(measured_error, "measured_error"),
499	               _probability(wrong_wrong_rate, "wrong_wrong_rate"))
500	    eta = _probability(eta, "eta")
501	    if not eta < HALF or not 1 - a - eta > 0:
502	        raise ValueError("eta must lie below one half and below 1 - a'")
503	    return (w * (1 - 2 * eta) - eta * (a - e)) / (1 - a - eta)
504	
505	
506	def _sensitivity_numerator(a: Q, e: Q, w: Q) -> Q:
507	    return w * (2 * a - 1) - (a - e) * (1 - a)
508	
509	
510	def eps1_sensitivity(measured_accuracy, measured_error, wrong_wrong_rate, eta) -> Q:
511	    """``d eps1 / d eta = K / (1 - a' - eta)^2`` with the ``eta``-free
512	    ``K = w (2a' - 1) - (a' - eps')(1 - a')``.  Proof: ``eps1 = N / D`` with
513	    ``N = w - eta (2w + a' - eps')`` and ``D = 1 - a' - eta`` both affine, so
514	    ``N' D - N D' = -(2w + a' - eps') D + N = K``."""
515	
516	    a, e, w = (_probability(measured_accuracy, "measured_accuracy"),
517	               _probability(measured_error, "measured_error"),
518	               _probability(wrong_wrong_rate, "wrong_wrong_rate"))
519	    eta = _probability(eta, "eta")
520	    if not eta < HALF or not 1 - a - eta > 0:
521	        raise ValueError("eta must lie below one half and below 1 - a'")
522	    return _sensitivity_numerator(a, e, w) / (1 - a - eta) ** 2
523	
524	
525	def eps1_displacement(measured_accuracy, measured_error, wrong_wrong_rate, eta, delta) -> Q:
526	    """Exact ``eps1(eta + delta) - eps1(eta) = delta K / (D(eta) D(eta + delta))``:
527	    the derivative's denominator with one factor moved to the displaced point."""
528	
529	    a, e, w = (_probability(measured_accuracy, "measured_accuracy"),
530	               _probability(measured_error, "measured_error"),
531	               _probability(wrong_wrong_rate, "wrong_wrong_rate"))
532	    eta, delta = _probability(eta, "eta"), _as_q(delta, "delta")
533	    moved = eta + delta
534	    if not 0 <= moved < HALF or not eta < HALF or not 1 - a - eta > 0 or not 1 - a - moved > 0:
535	        raise ValueError("eta and eta + delta must lie in [0, 1/2) and below 1 - a'")
536	    return delta * _sensitivity_numerator(a, e, w) / ((1 - a - eta) * (1 - a - moved))

551	def calibrate(record: RecordTable, declared_judge_error=None, alpha=Q(1, 20),
552	              resolution=RESOLUTION) -> dict[str, object]:
553	    """The pipeline.  From the 2^4 record: the label table's constraint check;
554	    ``eta1``, ``eta2`` and ``a`` from the three-rater identity (exact or
555	    bracketed); Proposition 2 inverted at ``eta1`` (at both bracket ends when
556	    bracketed -- every inverted rate is monotone in ``eta``, so the ends map
557	    to ends); the corrected expected counts rounded half-up; the judge
558	    module's exact tests on them; the sensitivity of ``eps1`` to ``eta1``.
559	
560	    The tests take the corrected counts as given.  They are an estimate, not a
561	    sample, so the sampling error of ``eta1`` is not in their p-values; the
562	    sensitivity is the first-order account of it."""
563	
564	    alpha = _probability(alpha, "alpha")
565	    declared = None if declared_judge_error is None else _probability(declared_judge_error, "declared_judge_error")
566	    labels = record.label_table()
567	    constraints = model_constraints(labels)
568	    measured = measured_judge_rates(record, 1)
569	    out = {"size": record.total, "constraints": constraints, "identifiable": constraints["identifiable"],
570	           "measured": measured, "declared_judge_error": declared}
571	    if not constraints["identifiable"]:
572	        out.update({"status": "not_identified", "eta1": None, "eta2": None, "accuracy_from_identity": None,
573	                    "inversions": [], "valid": False})
574	        return out
575	    squares = constraints["squares"]
576	    brackets = {i: error_rate_bracket(squares[i], resolution) for i in (1, 2, 3)}
577	    accuracy_identity = {"lower": 1 - brackets[3]["upper"], "upper": 1 - brackets[3]["lower"],
578	                         "exact": None if brackets[3]["exact"] is None else 1 - brackets[3]["exact"]}
579	    eta1 = brackets[1]
580	    points = [eta1["exact"]] if eta1["exact"] is not None else [eta1["lower"], eta1["upper"]]
581	    if record.total.denominator != 1:
582	        raise ValueError("corrected counts need an integer total")
583	    size = int(record.total)
584	    inversions = []
585	    for eta in points:
586	        rates = gold_noise_inverse(measured["accuracy"], measured["judge_error"], measured["eps1"], eta)
587	        closed = inverted_eps1(measured["accuracy"], measured["judge_error"], measured["wrong_wrong_rate"], eta)
588	        if closed != rates["eps1"]:
589	            raise AssertionError("closed-form inversion disagrees with the judge module")
590	        expected = expected_table(size, rates["accuracy"], rates["judge_error"], rates["eps1"])
591	        table, changed = rounded_table(expected)
592	        error = declared if declared is not None else rates["judge_error"]
593	        inversions.append({"eta": eta, "recovered": rates, "corrected_expected": expected,
594	                           "corrected_table": table, "rounding_changed_a_cell": changed,
595	                           "tests": _judge_tests(table, error, alpha, declared is None),

651	def root_bracket(value, bits: int = ROOT_BITS) -> dict[str, object]:
652	    """``sqrt(value)`` exactly when rational, else the bracket
653	    ``[r / 2^bits, (r + 1) / 2^bits)`` with ``r = isqrt(floor(value 4^bits))``:
654	    an exact integer statement, since ``floor(sqrt(floor(x))) = floor(sqrt(x))``
655	    for ``x >= 0``.  Agrees with the bisection bracket of ``error_rate_bracket``."""
656	
657	    value = _as_q(value, "value")
658	    if value < 0 or type(bits) is not int or bits < 1:
659	        raise ValueError("value must be nonnegative and bits a positive integer")
660	    exact = exact_square_root(value)
661	    if exact is not None:
662	        return {"lower": exact, "upper": exact, "exact": exact, "width": Q(0)}
663	    r = isqrt((value.numerator << (2 * bits)) // value.denominator)
664	    return {"lower": Q(r, 1 << bits), "upper": Q(r + 1, 1 << bits), "exact": None, "width": Q(1, 1 << bits)}

667	def agreement_patterns(table: LabelTable) -> dict[object, Q]:
668	    """Per item the agreement indicators ``(I_12, I_13, I_23)`` take one of
669	    four values, ``(1,1,1)`` (``"all"``), ``(1,0,0)``, ``(0,1,0)``, ``(0,0,1)``:
670	    two agreements force the third.  ``q_all = p(000) + p(111) = (1 + kappa_12
671	    + kappa_13 + kappa_23) / 4`` and ``q_ij = A_ij - q_all`` depend on the table
672	    only through the kappas, so under the model the law of any function of the
673	    agreement counts is free of the prior."""
674	
675	    q = {name: Q(0) for name in PATTERNS}
676	    for cell in CELLS3:
677	        a, b, c = cell
678	        key = "all" if a == b == c else (1, 2) if a == b else (1, 3) if a == c else (2, 3)
679	        q[key] += table.probability(cell)
680	    return q

683	def agreement_covariance(table: LabelTable) -> dict[tuple, Q]:
684	    """Per-item covariance of ``(I_12, I_13, I_23)``: ``Var I_ij = (1 -
685	    kappa_ij^2) / 4`` and ``Cov(I_ij, I_ik) = q_all - A_ij A_ik = (kappa_jk -
686	    kappa_ij kappa_ik) / 4`` for any distribution; the sample agreement rates
687	    on ``m`` items have covariance ``Sigma / m``.  Not diagonal."""
688	
689	    kappas = pairwise_kappas(table)
690	    q_all = agreement_patterns(table)["all"]
691	    return {(p, r): (1 - kappas[p] ** 2) / 4 if p == r else q_all - (1 + kappas[p]) * (1 + kappas[r]) / 4
692	            for p in PAIRS for r in PAIRS}

694	
695	def agreement_covariance_model(errors) -> dict[tuple, Q]:
696	    """The same matrix under the model: ``Cov(I_ij, I_ik) = d_j d_k (1 - d_i^2) / 4``
697	    (``kappa_jk - kappa_ij kappa_ik = d_j d_k - d_i^2 d_j d_k``) and
698	    ``Var I_ij = (1 - d_i^2 d_j^2) / 4``."""
699	
700	    d = {i + 1: 1 - 2 * e for i, e in enumerate(_three(errors, "errors"))}
701	    out = {}
702	    for p in PAIRS:
703	        for r in PAIRS:
704	            if p == r:
705	                out[(p, r)] = (1 - (d[p[0]] * d[p[1]]) ** 2) / 4
706	            else:
707	                (i,) = set(p) & set(r)
708	                j, k = _others(i)
709	                out[(p, r)] = d[j] * d[k] * (1 - d[i] ** 2) / 4
710	    return out

713	def delta_variance(errors) -> dict[str, object]:
714	    """Asymptotic ``m Var(eta1_hat) -> V = g^T Sigma g`` with the gradient per
715	    agreement rate ``g = (-1/(2 d_2), -1/(2 d_3), d_1/(2 d_2 d_3))`` (twice the
716	    per-kappa gradient of ``eta_gradient``) and ``Sigma`` the model covariance:
717	
718	    ``V = (d_1^2 + d_2^2 + d_3^2 - 2 d_1^2 d_2^2 - 2 d_1^2 d_3^2 + 2 d_2^2 d_3^2
719	    - d_1^2 d_2^2 d_3^2) / (16 d_2^2 d_3^2)``.
720	
721	    The square ``S = (1 - 2 eta_1)^2 = kappa_12 kappa_13 / kappa_23`` has
722	    gradient ``-4 d_1 g``, so ``m Var(S_hat) -> 16 d_1^2 V``.  Every rater
723	    must be better than chance: at ``d_1 = 0`` the root is not differentiable
724	    and the estimator is undefined with probability bounded away from zero."""
725	
726	    errors = _three(errors, "errors")
727	    d1, d2, d3 = (1 - 2 * e for e in errors)
728	    if not (d1 > 0 and d2 > 0 and d3 > 0):
729	        raise ValueError("the delta method needs every error rate below one half")
730	    gradient = {(1, 2): -1 / (2 * d2), (1, 3): -1 / (2 * d3), (2, 3): d1 / (2 * d2 * d3)}
731	    sigma = agreement_covariance_model(errors)
732	    quadratic = sum((gradient[p] * sigma[(p, r)] * gradient[r] for p in PAIRS for r in PAIRS), Q(0))
733	    numerator = (d1 ** 2 + d2 ** 2 + d3 ** 2 - 2 * d1 ** 2 * d2 ** 2 - 2 * d1 ** 2 * d3 ** 2
734	                 + 2 * d2 ** 2 * d3 ** 2 - d1 ** 2 * d2 ** 2 * d3 ** 2)
735	    closed = numerator / (16 * d2 ** 2 * d3 ** 2)
736	    if closed != quadratic:
737	        raise AssertionError("closed form of the delta variance disagrees with g^T Sigma g")
738	    return {"eta": closed, "square": 16 * d1 ** 2 * closed, "gradient_per_agreement_rate": gradient,
739	            "covariance": sigma, "numerator": numerator, "root_of_eta_variance": exact_square_root(closed)}
740

772	def _law_summary(m: int, eta1: Q, tolerance: Q, bits: int, total: int, w: dict, acc_num: dict,
773	                 acc_num2: dict, acc_root: int, square_distribution: dict | None) -> dict[str, object]:
774	    w_def = w["exact"] + w["bracketed"]
775	    out = {"size": m, "eta1": eta1, "tolerance": tolerance,

780	           "p_within_tolerance_given_defined": None if w_def == 0 else Q(w["within"], w_def)}

782	        out.update({"square_mean": None, "square_variance": None})

785	    es2 = sum((Q(v, (m * d) ** 2) for d, v in acc_num2.items()), Q(0)) / w_def
786	    root_lo, root_hi = Q(acc_root, w_def << bits), Q(acc_root + w_def, w_def << bits)
787	    out.update({"square_mean": es, "square_variance": es2 - es * es, "scaled_square_variance": m * (es2 - es * es),
788	                "root_mean_bracket": (root_lo, root_hi),
789	                "eta_mean_bracket": ((1 - root_hi) / 2, (1 - root_lo) / 2),
790	                "eta_variance_bracket": ((es - root_hi ** 2) / 4, (es - root_lo ** 2) / 4),
791	                "scaled_eta_variance_bracket": (m * (es - root_hi ** 2) / 4, m * (es - root_lo ** 2) / 4),
792	                "moments_are": "conditional on the estimator being defined",
793	                "square_distribution": square_distribution})
794	    return out

797	def _tolerance_bounds(eta1: Q, tolerance: Q) -> tuple[Q, Q]:
798	    """``|eta_hat - eta1| <= tol`` iff ``lo <= S_hat <= hi`` with ``lo = max(0,
799	    1 - 2(eta1 + tol))^2`` and ``hi = min(1, 1 - 2(eta1 - tol))^2``."""
800	
801	    low_root, high_root = max(Q(0), 1 - 2 * (eta1 + tolerance)), min(Q(1), 1 - 2 * (eta1 - tolerance))
802	    return low_root ** 2, high_root ** 2

805	def sampling_law(size, errors, tolerance=Q(1, 50), bits: int = ROOT_BITS) -> dict[str, object]:
806	    """Exact law of ``eta1_hat`` on ``m`` items, free of the prior, by
807	    enumerating the ``C(m+3, 3)`` compositions of the four-category multinomial
808	    of agreement patterns (integer weights over a common denominator ``D^m``).
809	
810	    Outcome classes: some ``kappa_hat <= 0`` (sign; undefined), all positive
811	    but ``S_hat > 1`` (range; undefined), ``S_hat`` a perfect square (exact
812	    ``eta1_hat``) and otherwise (bracketed).  Moments of ``S_hat`` and of
813	    ``eta1_hat`` are conditional on the defined event; those of ``eta1_hat``
814	    are brackets, from ``root_bracket`` at ``2^-bits`` per outcome.  Also the
815	    exact probability that the estimator is defined and within ``tolerance``
816	    of ``eta1``."""
817	
818	    m, errors, tolerance = _size(size), _three(errors, "errors"), _probability(tolerance, "tolerance")
819	    n, den = _pattern_integers(errors)
820	    n0, n12, n13, n23 = n["all"], n[(1, 2)], n[(1, 3)], n[(2, 3)]
821	    pw = {name: [1] * (m + 1) for name in ("0", "12", "13", "23")}
822	    for name, base in (("0", n0), ("12", n12), ("13", n13), ("23", n23)):
823	        for k in range(1, m + 1):
824	            pw[name][k] = pw[name][k - 1] * base
825	    fact = [factorial(k) for k in range(m + 1)]
826	    choose = [[comb(r, j) for j in range(r + 1)] for r in range(m + 1)]
827	    lo_sq, hi_sq = _tolerance_bounds(errors[0], tolerance)
828	    lo_n, lo_d, hi_n, hi_d = lo_sq.numerator, lo_sq.denominator, hi_sq.numerator, hi_sq.denominator
829	    shift = 2 * bits
830	    w = {"sign": 0, "range": 0, "exact": 0, "bracketed": 0, "within": 0}
831	    acc_num, acc_num2, acc_root, total = {}, {}, 0, 0
832	    for k23 in range(m + 1):
833	        for k0 in range(m - k23 + 1):
834	            rest = m - k23 - k0
835	            d = 2 * (k0 + k23) - m
836	            dd = m * d
837	            outer = fact[m] // (fact[k23] * fact[k0] * fact[rest]) * pw["23"][k23] * pw["0"][k0]
838	            row, p12, p13 = choose[rest], pw["12"], pw["13"]
839	            s_num = s_num2 = 0
840	            for k12 in range(rest + 1):
841	                weight = outer * row[k12] * p12[k12] * p13[rest - k12]
842	                total += weight
843	                a, b = 2 * (k0 + k12) - m, 2 * (k0 + rest - k12) - m
844	                if a <= 0 or b <= 0 or d <= 0:
845	                    w["sign"] += weight
846	                    continue
847	                num = a * b
848	                if num > dd:
849	                    w["range"] += weight
850	                    continue
851	                s_num += weight * num
852	                s_num2 += weight * num * num
853	                g = gcd(num, dd)
854	                nn, dn = num // g, dd // g
855	                rn, rd = isqrt(nn), isqrt(dn)
856	                w["exact" if rn * rn == nn and rd * rd == dn else "bracketed"] += weight
857	                if num * lo_d >= lo_n * dd and num * hi_d <= hi_n * dd:
858	                    w["within"] += weight
859	                acc_root += weight * isqrt((num << shift) // dd)
860	            if s_num:
861	                acc_num[d] = acc_num.get(d, 0) + s_num
862	                acc_num2[d] = acc_num2.get(d, 0) + s_num2
863	    if total != den ** m:
864	        raise AssertionError("the multinomial weights do not sum to D^m")
865	    out = _law_summary(m, errors[0], tolerance, bits, total, w, acc_num, acc_num2, acc_root, None)
866	    out.update({"method": "four-pattern multinomial", "compositions": comb(m + 3, 3),
867	                "pattern_probabilities": {str(k): Q(v, den) for k, v in n.items()}})
868	    return out

871	def sampling_law_by_tables(size, errors, tolerance=Q(1, 50), bits: int = ROOT_BITS) -> dict[str, object]:
872	    """The same law by enumerating every label table, ``C(m+7, 7)`` of them,
873	    with the full distribution of ``S_hat`` on the defined event: the
874	    cross-check of the four-pattern reduction."""
875	
876	    m, errors, tolerance = _size(size), _three(errors, "errors"), _probability(tolerance, "tolerance")
877	    table = three_rater_model(HALF, errors)
878	    den = 1
879	    for cell in CELLS3:
880	        den = den * table.probability(cell).denominator // gcd(den, table.probability(cell).denominator)
881	    n = [int(table.probability(cell) * den) for cell in CELLS3]
882	    pw = [[base ** k for k in range(m + 1)] for base in n]
883	    fact = [factorial(k) for k in range(m + 1)]
884	    patterns = [(int(a == b), int(a == c), int(b == c)) for a, b, c in CELLS3]
885	    lo_sq, hi_sq = _tolerance_bounds(errors[0], tolerance)
886	    w = {"sign": 0, "range": 0, "exact": 0, "bracketed": 0, "within": 0}
887	    acc_num, acc_num2, acc_root, total, distribution = {}, {}, 0, 0, {}
888	    shift = 2 * bits
889	
890	    def visit(counts: list[int]) -> None:
891	        nonlocal acc_root, total
892	        weight, n12, n13, n23 = fact[m], 0, 0, 0
893	        for j, k in enumerate(counts):
894	            weight = weight // fact[k] * pw[j][k]
895	            n12 += patterns[j][0] * k
896	            n13 += patterns[j][1] * k
897	            n23 += patterns[j][2] * k
898	        total += weight
899	        a, b, d = 2 * n12 - m, 2 * n13 - m, 2 * n23 - m
900	        if a <= 0 or b <= 0 or d <= 0:
901	            w["sign"] += weight
902	            return
903	        square = Q(a * b, m * d)
904	        if square > 1:
905	            w["range"] += weight
906	            return
907	        distribution[square] = distribution.get(square, 0) + weight
908	        acc_num[d] = acc_num.get(d, 0) + weight * a * b
909	        acc_num2[d] = acc_num2.get(d, 0) + weight * (a * b) ** 2
910	        w["exact" if exact_square_root(square) is not None else "bracketed"] += weight
911	        if lo_sq <= square <= hi_sq:
912	            w["within"] += weight
913	        acc_root += weight * isqrt((a * b << shift) // (m * d))
914	
915	    def compositions(i: int, remaining: int, counts: list[int]) -> None:
916	        if i == 7:
917	            visit(counts + [remaining])
918	            return
919	        for k in range(remaining + 1):
920	            compositions(i + 1, remaining - k, counts + [k])
921	
922	    compositions(0, m, [])
923	    if total != den ** m:
924	        raise AssertionError("the multinomial weights do not sum to D^m")
925	    out = _law_summary(m, errors[0], tolerance, bits, total, w, acc_num, acc_num2, acc_root,
926	                       {s: Q(c, total) for s, c in sorted(distribution.items())})
927	    out.update({"method": "all label tables", "compositions": comb(m + 7, 7)})
928	    return out

931	def _binomial_upper_tail(trials: int, p: Q, k: int) -> Q:
932	    """``P(Bin(n, p) >= k)`` by integer accumulation over the common
933	    denominator ``b^n`` (``p = a/b``, ``c = b - a``): the terms ``t_j = C(n, j)
934	    a^j c^(n-j)`` satisfy ``t_{j+1} = t_j (n - j) a / ((j + 1) c)`` exactly, so
935	    one small multiplication and one exact small division per term.  Equals
936	    the judge module's tail."""
937	
938	    a, b = p.numerator, p.denominator
939	    c = b - a
940	    if k <= 0:
941	        return Q(1)
942	    if k > trials or a == 0:
943	        return Q(0)
944	    if c == 0:
945	        return Q(1)
946	    term = comb(trials, k) * a ** k * c ** (trials - k)
947	    acc = term
948	    for j in range(k, trials):
949	        term = term * (trials - j) * a // ((j + 1) * c)
950	        acc += term
951	    return Q(acc, b ** trials)

954	def disagreement_bound(size, agreements, alpha=Q(1, 20), resolution=RESOLUTION) -> dict[str, object]:
955	    """An exact conservative confidence statement from ``N_12`` alone, which
956	    is ``Bin(m, A_12)`` with ``A_12 = (1 + d_1 d_2) / 2`` whenever G1 and G2
957	    are conditionally independent (the controller is not needed).  With the
958	    one-sided lower Clopper-Pearson endpoint ``A_L`` (``P[Bin(m, A_L) >= N_12]
959	    = alpha``), ``d_1 d_2 >= 2 A_L - 1`` at confidence ``1 - alpha``, and since
960	    ``d_2 <= 1``: ``eta_1 <= 1 - A_L``, likewise ``eta_2 <= 1 - A_L``.  It bounds
961	    each grader's error by the pair's disagreement; it gives no lower bound,
962	    does not separate ``eta_1`` from ``eta_2``, ignores the controller, and is
963	    tight only when the other grader is perfect.  ``A_L`` is a beta quantile,
964	    bracketed to ``resolution`` by bisection on the exact tail."""
965	
966	    m, alpha, resolution = _size(size), _probability(alpha, "alpha"), _as_q(resolution, "resolution")
967	    if type(agreements) is not int or not 0 <= agreements <= m:
968	        raise ValueError("agreements must be an integer count between 0 and size")
969	    if not 0 < alpha < 1 or resolution <= 0:
970	        raise ValueError("alpha must lie strictly inside (0, 1) and resolution be positive")
971	    if agreements == 0:
972	        low = high = Q(0)
973	    else:
974	        low, high = Q(0), Q(1)
975	        while high - low > resolution:
976	            mid = (low + high) / 2
977	            if _binomial_upper_tail(m, mid, agreements) < alpha:
978	                low = mid
979	            else:
980	                high = mid
981	    return {"size": m, "agreements": agreements, "alpha": alpha, "agreement_rate": Q(agreements, m),
982	            "lower_endpoint_bracket": (low, high), "eta_upper_bound": 1 - low,
983	            "eta_upper_bound_at_population_rate": 1 - Q(agreements, m),
984	            "bounds": "eta_1 and eta_2 each, from above only; valid without the controller"}

1017	def dawid_skene_moments(table: LabelTable) -> dict[str, object]:
1018	    """``p_i = P[X_i = 1]``, the pair covariances ``c_ij = p_ij - p_i p_j`` and
1019	    the third central moment ``k_3 = E prod (X_i - p_i) = p_123 - sum_i p_i
1020	    p_jk + 2 p_1 p_2 p_3``.  Under the model, with ``u = pi (1 - pi)`` and
1021	    ``delta_i = 1 - alpha_i - beta_i``: ``c_ij = u delta_i delta_j`` (rank one)
1022	    and ``k_3 = u (1 - 2 pi) delta_1 delta_2 delta_3``, so the radicand
1023	    ``k_3^2 + 4 c_12 c_13 c_23 = (u delta_1 delta_2 delta_3)^2``."""
1024	
1025	    p = {i: sum((table.probability(c) for c in CELLS3 if c[i - 1] == 1), Q(0)) for i in (1, 2, 3)}
1026	    pp = {pair: sum((table.probability(c) for c in CELLS3 if c[pair[0] - 1] == 1 and c[pair[1] - 1] == 1), Q(0))
1027	          for pair in PAIRS}
1028	    p123 = table.probability((1, 1, 1))
1029	    cov = {pair: pp[pair] - p[pair[0]] * p[pair[1]] for pair in PAIRS}
